chunks: Ali ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas al-Baghdadi (in Ray), known as Abu al-Hasan al-Hanuti, narrated to us; he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn [Ahmad ibn] Sulayman ibn al-Harith narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf al-Attar narrated to us; he said: al-Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us; he said: I said to Hisham ibn al-Hakam: What is the meaning of your saying: 'The Imam is not but Infallible'? He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, to which he said: The Infallible is the one who refrains, through Allah, from all the prohibitions of Allah. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: 'And he who adheres to Allah, has certainly been guided to a Straight Path.'

key_terms.إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا مَعْ: The Imam is not but Infallible
key_terms.وَمَنْ يَعْتَصِمِ بِاللَّهِ: And he who adheres to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the theological definition of an Infallible Imam in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Hisham ibn al-Hakam reports Imam al-Sadiq defining the Imam as 'al-Ma'sum'—one divinely prevented from sin—by linking this state to holding fast to Allah. This establishes the theological basis for the Imam's infallibility as a necessary condition for his role as the perfect guide, ensuring his teachings remain free from error. The concept underscores the Shia belief that divine protection (Ismah) is intrinsic to the Imam's authority and spiritual perfection.
